question: Our signed-token validation occasionally crashes with an unexpected Python exception. Investigate the root cause using our company knowledge and fix it.

published_claims.text: The source exposes a crash path in TimestampSigner.unsign: a valid signature can contain an unrepresentable timestamp. Conversion errors are normalized only in the invalid-signature branch; valid-signature conversions can leak ValueError, OSError or OverflowError.
This affects validate(), which catches only BadSignature, and timed serializer loads(), which always requests timestamp conversion.

Recommended fix: in unsign(), convert every decoded timestamp once under the existing three-exception guard, raising BadTimeSignature("Malformed timestamp", payload=value) on failure. Reuse the converted datetime for expiration errors and timestamp returns, including checking representability when no timestamp return is requested.

Add deterministic regression tests using a mocked timestamp of 10**12: cover unsign(), timestamp returns, max_age, validate() returning False, and timed serializer loads(). Preserve normal UTC timestamps, expiration behavior and tampered-token rejection.

disclosure: Fresh session; no filenames, symbols or document names in the user prompt. Reviewed synthetic demo memory seeds were available. Published answer cites company code and documents; memory retrieval alone does not prove causal contribution. Separate memory-guided plan follows.
